key_claims: Sleep does not isolate the brain from the world; it affects how the brain balances processing of different types of sensory information.
During REM sleep, signals from the outside world gradually decrease.
During REM sleep, signals from the body are preserved or even enhanced.
The study was conducted by scientists from the universities of Lausanne and Geneva.
The study offers a partial explanation for the phenomenon.
limitations: The source does not specify the exact number of participants or the methods used.
The source does not detail the specific types of sensory signals measured.
The source does not provide the full context of the study design or statistical significance.
The source does not mention any potential confounding factors or alternative explanations.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that the brain completely ignores the outside world during REM sleep.
The study identifies the exact neural mechanisms responsible for the shift in sensory processing.
The study applies to all stages of sleep, not just REM.
The study provides a complete explanation for why dreams occur.
The study was conducted by a single university.
